questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belarus?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belarus article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belarus?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belarus on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belarus article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Belarus?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belarus article.

questions.proof: The country has two official languages: Belarusian and Russian.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Belarus has four World Heritage Sites: the Mir Castle Complex, the Nesvizh Castle, the Belovezhskaya Pushcha (shared with _____), and the Struve Geodetic Arc (shared with nine other countries).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “shared”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “World Heritage Sites” part of the Belarus article.

questions.proof: Belarus has four World Heritage Sites: the Mir Castle Complex, the Nesvizh Castle, the Belovezhskaya Pushcha (shared with Poland), and the Struve Geodetic Arc (shared with nine other countries).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The land stayed with _____ until going to the German Empire during World War I.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “until”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Prior to First World War” part of the Belarus article.

questions.proof: The land stayed with Russia until going to the German Empire during World War I.
